(i) it is possible to publish ${\mbox{LaTeX}}$ documents as Linked Data, (ii) this can be done in a way that allows for a seamless interaction of students with the documents, and (iii) it can be done in an extensible way, so that the corpus can be linked to other sites.
(i) it is feasible to publish math lecture notes as Linked Data and (ii) it is feasible for students to interactively browse the resulting documents.

we have created a Linked Data corpus of lecture notes that is browsable and searchable, and that is a step towards an integrated Linked Data ecosystem.
we have created a corpus of linked lecture notes, which are accessible via a web interface and can be queried by students, lecturers, and search engines.
our approach is a first step in the direction towards a semantic Web.

we show that the combination of ${\m box{\LaTeX}}$, RDF and MathML is feasible and can be useful for the Semantic Web.

the use of ${\m box{\LaTeX}}$, a widely used tool for writing mathematical documents, is compatible with the Linked Data paradigm, and can lead to the creation of a large corpus of semantically enhanced documents.
